title: Spread an order discount across its lines, to the cent
examObjective: Predicting the result of core DataWeave functions
basics: Splitting an amount in proportion to other amounts produces fractions of a cent, and rounding each share on its own can make the shares add up to a cent more or less than the whole. The usual fix is to round every share down and then hand the leftover cents to chosen lines.
prompt:
An order has lines `{ sku, amount }` (amounts in cents) and a `discount` in cents. Spread the discount across the lines in proportion to their amounts:

1. each line gets `floor(discount * amount / total)`, where `total` is the sum of the line amounts;
2. whatever is left over after that goes, in full, to the **first line with the largest amount**.

Return `{ sku, discount }` per line. The discounts must add up exactly to the order discount.
hints: Work out the rounded-down shares first, and from them the leftover.
Rounding each share to the nearest cent does not guarantee the total. Check the second hidden case.
Find the position of the largest line with `(amounts indexOf max(amounts))`, then add the leftover to the share at that position.

mustFail.why: rounds each share to the nearest cent, so the shares can add up to more than the discount
gives the leftover to the first line rather than the largest one

explanation.approach: Rounding every share independently is where cents appear from nowhere: 99 split 50/25/25 rounds to 50, 25 and 25, which is 100. Rounding every share down and handing out the difference guarantees the total. The sample divides evenly, so neither mistake shows until the hidden orders.

snippets.label: Independent rounding
snippets.note: Adds up to 100, one cent more than the discount.
